title: SoK: Grading Open-Text Legal Answers, from Law School Exams to Trustworthy Rubric Judges
abstract: arXiv:2610.19992v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Law students are examined through open-text answers: case solutions, essays and memos that apply the law to a set of facts. Such answers are expensive to grade, human graders disagree widely on them, and large language models (LLMs) now offer to grade them at scale, both in teaching and in the benchmarks that test legal AI. This paper systematizes how open-text legal answers can be evaluated. We derive eight desiderata from educational measurement and from the law that governs exams, among them validity, reliability, reasons, credit for defensible alternative solutions, robustness to gaming and human oversight. We then compare eight evaluation paradigms against them, from unstructured human grading to LLM judges with instance-specific rubrics and pairwise comparison. Three findings stand out. translated_title: SoK：开放式法律文本答案的评分——从法学院考试到可信赖的评分规则裁判
translated_abstract: 法学学生通过开放式文本答案接受考核：案例分析、论文和法律备忘录，将法律适用于一组特定事实。这类答案的评分成本高昂，人类评分者之间分歧很大，而大型语言模型（LLM）如今可以在教学中以及测试法律AI的基准评测中大规模进行评分。本文系统化地研究了如何评估开放式法律文本答案。我们从教育测量学以及规范考试的法律中推导出八项必要条件，其中包括效度、信度、说理依据、对可辩护的替代解答给予得分、对投机取巧行为的鲁棒性以及人类监督。随后，我们将八种评估范式与这些标准进行对比，范围涵盖从非结构化的人工评分，到采用针对具体实例的评分规则的LLM裁判，再到成对比较。有三个发现尤为突出。为任务量身编写的评分规则是使LLM裁判与人类评分者达成一致的最强杠杆，但所报告的数字回答的是不同的问题……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 本文系统化研究了开放式法律文本答案（如法学院考试）的评估方法，从教育测量与法律规范中提炼出八项评估标准并对比八种评估范式，发现针对任务定制评分规则是让LLM裁判与人类评分者达成一致的最关键手段。
en_tdlr: This SoK paper systematizes the evaluation of open-text legal answers by deriving eight desiderata from educational measurement and law and comparing eight evaluation paradigms, finding that task-specific rubrics are the strongest lever for aligning LLM judges with human graders.
